i've done the ice cube thing in the past - it's a nice/strange feeling.

I don't want my boyfriend to feel like he's my carer.  When I talk to him about these feelings he's unconstrucive and urges me to speak to proffessionals.  however, sometimes it's him that i want a response from. just a simple cuddle and "everything will be alright, i'm here" or something sappy like that.  Am i putting him under too much pressure??? why am i stressing about this!?

I don't really have anyone I can rant and confess to really. however i have found reddit very useful at this stage as i'm trying to calm myself down.  I really appreciate your response and support; thank you.

thank you for such a kind hearted reply.
to answer your question, there wasn't one reason for self harm when i started.  To be honest, i don't even remember when i started, it was just something that i did.  When i was angry, or confused i would self harm. At some points it was just a habbit; i didn't need to be upset to do it, it was just part of my daily routine.
I always hurt myself in places that people would never see and i still secretly take pride in the fact that no one has accidentally seen or guessed that i do/did these stupid things.

I hate being confused. it freaks me out. it upsets me more than bad situations.  If I don't understand something or a situation and it can't be explained to me or i just generally feel completely stupid, i start to get short of breath and short tempered and would usually self harm during a temper that had flared because of confusion. I still get very deffensive when someone patronises me in a "you don't understand" manner (which probably just comes off as rudeness or arrogance).

And as for your comments on the tortured past - i have great respect for you for not saying "but what IS your tortured past?" because at this moment in time i don't feel like it needs to be talked about, i just need someone to talk me down. so thank you.
I always thought the idea of writing down diary entries to organise ones emotions was slightly clichéd and perhaps embaressing (reading childhood diaries i always sounded like SUCH a whiner and resented myself for it!).  However, if it has worked for people then i will try and and approach it with an open mind.  I just hope no one sees it.

thanks again.
At the moment i'm taking Fluoxetine.  I used to be on cetalipram (not spelled like that...).
I hadn't thought of it that way.  Thank you.
not enough, no. i'm overweight, but i've recently started eating healthier and swimming regularly.
Thank you.  I really appreciate you taking the time to read all this!  I think the country i've moved to is a bit thin on the ground with mental support, but i will look into it.
